answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to give every agent a ferrous core of verifiable history: each identity carries a cipher-signed chain of completed tasks that peers can audit, and reputation is earned slowly, task by task. A long-lived relic of honest work — years of cross-checked trades — cannot be minted overnight, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs more than the access they would gain, while honest agents keep the standing they built and misbehaviour burns it away.
